papers.title: Quantum Simulation of Hadronization: From String Breaking to Event Generation
papers.abstract: High-energy collisions produce large numbers of quarks and gluons that are bound into hadrons by the confining interactions of quantum chromodynamics (QCD). This hadronization process is intrinsically real-time and non-perturbative. Event generators describe hadronization using phenomenological models with parameters fitted to data rather than calculated from QCD. Uncertainties in these models limit the precision of certain measurements at the Large Hadron Collider. Quantum computers could enable first-principles simulations of these dynamics. Existing quantum simulations of gauge theories have demonstrated string-breaking dynamics. This white paper summarizes the conclusions of the InQubator for Quantum Simulation workshop \textit{From String Dynamics to Event Generation with Quantum Simulation}. We develop a roadmap for extending these simulations to inform phenomenological models of hadronization. A sequence of toy models is proposed for connecting current quantum simulations to QCD. The observables that should be extracted are listed, and the challenges that separate present simulations from quantitative predictions are identified. We propose a staged program in which quantum simulations first provide qualitative modifications to event generators and later provide quantitative input.
papers.reason: A major white paper exploring quantum simulations of string breaking and hadronization for event generators, highly relevant to neutrino and collider physics modeling. [favorite author: Mrenna]

summary.tldr: This white paper develops a roadmap for using quantum simulations of gauge theories to model the non-perturbative real-time dynamics of hadronization and constrain event-generator parameters.
summary.novel_idea: Unlike Euclidean lattice methods restricted to static correlators or tensor networks limited by entanglement, this work outlines how near-term and fault-tolerant quantum hardware can compute real-time string-breaking and soft-function matrix elements to directly test the assumptions of Lund and cluster fragmentation models.
summary.method: The authors synthesize findings from an IQuS workshop, proposing a hierarchy of toy models ($Z_2$, U(1), and non-Abelian SU($N$) lattice gauge theories) with staggered or dressed-site fermion encodings. They investigate state preparation, Trotterized time evolution, gauge-invariant encodings, and observable extraction (momentum, flavor, entanglement, and magic).
key_results: Identified hadronization parameter uncertainties as a dominant LHC systematic (e.g., 50% spread in identified-particle spectra, underpredicted charm baryon ratios).
Established that SU(2) and Abelian lattice simulations have reached $	extgreater 100$ qubits, making qualitative modifications to event generators a near-term goal.
Outlined resource requirements and algorithmic strategies for transitioning from toy models to $(2+1)$D and $(3+1)$D QCD implementations.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly relevant to your interest in neutrino event generators (GENIE, GiBUU, etc.) and their underlying non-perturbative physics models, as well as the intersection of quantum simulation with hadronic final-state interactions and intranuclear cascades.
summary.caveats: Direct simulation of an end-to-end collider event remains infeasible ($n_L 	extgreater 10^{15}$ for the LHC), so the framework relies on matching isolated non-perturbative sub-processes (like string breaking) to phenomenological generator tunes.

papers.title: World average charged-current inclusive neutrino cross section from 6 to 200 GeV
papers.abstract:
The methods of the Particle Data Group are applied to produce a world average inclusive, charged-current, muon neutrino cross section energy-dependence slope $\sigma/E_
u$ . For the energy range $30 < E_
u < 200$, values obtained are (0.677 $\pm$ 0.013) and (0.335 $\pm$ 0.007) $	imes 10^{-38}$ cm$^2$/GeV for neutrino and anti-neutrino, respectively. These values are practically identical to those in common use. This paper expands the experiments whose data are used and describes the evolution of measurements leading to the result. Next, the value for $\sigma/E_
u$ is obtained for the low energy extensions by experiments that used the low-$
u$ method to anchor to the high energy result. In the range $6 < E_
u < 30$ GeV, values of (0.698 $\pm$ 0.018) and (0.316 $\pm$ 0.012) $	imes 10^{-38}$ cm$^2$/GeV are obtained. These are higher than the high energy average for neutrino and lower for anti-neutrino, but consistent at the edge of the uncertainty estimates. An interpretation of the evolution of the inclusive cross section, nuclear effects, and isoscalar corrections is provided in the context of the Bodek Yang 2000 model and two configurations of the GENIE neutrino event generators. These cross sections underpin foundational neutrino quantities such as structure functions, electroweak parameter measurements, and oscillation parameter determinations.

papers.title: Evaluation of $2\nu\beta\beta$ decay nuclear matrix elements using Lanczos techniques preserving Gamow-Teller strengths from both parent and daughter nuclei
papers.abstract:
We present two efficient shell-model approaches for calculating nuclear matrix elements (NMEs) for two-neutrino double-beta ($2
u eta eta$) decay and two-neutrino double-electron capture ($2
u$ECEC), based on the Lanczos strength-function and block-Lanczos techniques. The dual-sided Lanczos strength-function (DLSF) and block-Lanczos strength-function (BLSF) methods avoid the explicit calculation of a complete set of exact intermediate $1^+$ eigenstates and yield fully converged NMEs with a relatively small number of iterations starting from Gamow--Teller (GT) doorway states. Both methods simultaneously preserve the total GT strengths associated with the initial and final nuclei. We benchmark the methods for $^{48}$Ca in the $fp$ shell and apply them to candidates in different mass regions, including $^{58}$Ni, $^{76}$Ge, and $^{130}$Te. For $^{48}$Ca, a calculation allowing cross-shell excitations of up to $2\hbar\omega$ in the $sdpf$ model space yields a $2
u eta eta$ NME closer to the experimental estimate than the result obtained in the $fp$ shell. For $^{58}$Ni, we present, to our knowledge, the first shell-model calculation of the $2
u eta^+$EC/$2
u$ECEC NME. Comparison with the current experimental upper limit on the NME indicates the need for a more sensitive measurement of the $2
u eta^+$EC half-life. As an independent validation, the energy-denominator-free sums obtained with the proposed methods are compared with the corresponding double-GT matrix elements calculated directly between the initial and final ground states. Their agreement demonstrates that the methods correctly recover the complete energy-denominator-free intermediate-state sums.
papers.reason: Develops Lanczos strength-function methods for exact nuclear matrix elements in double-beta decay, directly touching core nuclear structure for neutrino processes.

summary.tldr:
The authors introduce two efficient shell-model Lanczos methods for calculating $2
u eta eta$ and $2
u	ext{ECEC}$ nuclear matrix elements that avoid intermediate-state summations while preserving total Gamow-Teller strengths for both parent and daughter nuclei.
summary.novel_idea: Unlike standard single-sided Lanczos strength-function (SLSF) approaches that only conserve Gamow-Teller sum rules for one side of the decay, the dual-sided Lanczos strength-function (DLSF) and block-Lanczos strength-function (BLSF) methods symmetrically preserve total GT strengths from both initial and final nuclei simultaneously.
summary.method: Using the KSHELL code, the authors apply Löwdin orthogonalization and subspace rediagonalization (DLSF) or block Krylov subspace iterations (BLSF) starting from GT doorway states. They benchmark the framework in the $fp$ shell for $^{48}	ext{Ca}$ and extend it to larger model spaces ($sdpf$, $f_5pg_9$, and $g_7ds	ext{-}h_{11}$) for $^{58}	ext{Ni}$, $^{76}	ext{Ge}$, and $^{130}	ext{Te}$.
key_results:
Fully converged $2
u eta eta$ NMEs are obtained with only $	extsim 30	ext{--}110$ iterations, bypassing the need to compute thousands of exact intermediate $1^+$ eigenstates.
For $^{48}	ext{Ca}$, cross-shell excitations up to $2	ext{--} ar{h}	ext{	extomega}$ in the $sdpf$ model space yield an NME closer to the NEMO-3 experimental estimate than the $fp$-shell calculation.

Presented the first shell-model calculation of the $2
u eta^+	ext{EC}/2
u	ext{ECEC}$ NME for $^{58}	ext{Ni}$ ($M_{2
u}  0.1250$), showing it lies two orders of magnitude below current experimental upper limits.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly relevant to your interest in ab initio and shell-model electroweak nuclear responses, nuclear matrix elements for double-beta decay, and methods to accurately capture high-lying GT strength distributions without prohibitive computational scaling.
summary.caveats:
Spurious center-of-mass excitations in enlarged model spaces (like $sdpf$) require careful filtering (e.g., Lawson prescription with $ eta_{	ext{cm}} = 10$), and extension to $0
u eta eta$ requires handling momentum-dependent neutrino potentials.

papers.title: Tests of an EP-Preserving Wake Force
papers.abstract: A universal quadratic coupling of ultralight scalar dark matter to ordinary matter preserves the weak equivalence principle for unscreened point particles. A finite test body is nevertheless not a passive probe: it distorts the scalar field that accelerates it. We show that this field distortion produces a differential acceleration between concentric test masses, even when their microscopic coupling is universal. We calculate this signal including how each test mass distorts the field acting on the other, deriving the weak-screening limit and extending the calculation to stronger screening using concentric spherical layers. Applying the model to MICROSCOPE, we find differential signals in both its equivalence-principle sensor SUEP, whose test masses have different compositions, and its reference sensor SUREF, whose test masses have the same composition. We combine both sensors with the dark matter wake near Earth to recast the published MICROSCOPE measurements. Within this model, existing measurements probe scalar masses up to approximately $8 \times 10^{-9}\,$eV and couplings below the supernova bound. An analysis using the additional frequency components of the scalar signal could extend the mass reach and probe couplings below the BBN bound.
papers.reason: Calculates finite test-body wake forces for universal quadratic scalar dark matter and recasts MICROSCOPE constraints, highly relevant to precision dark matter probes. [favorite author: Abhishek Banerjee]

summary.tldr: The authors demonstrate that universal quadratic couplings of ultralight scalar dark matter generate a differential wake force between concentric test masses due to mutual field distortion, enabling tests with equivalence-principle experiments like MICROSCOPE.
summary.novel_idea: Even though a universal microscopic coupling preserves the weak equivalence principle for point particles, finite concentric bodies distort the ambient scalar field differently, allowing experiments designed for composition-dependent tests (such as MICROSCOPE's reference sensor SUREF) to constrain universally coupled scalar dark matter.
summary.method: The authors derive the field profile and weak-screening limit using a concentric spherical-shell approximation for the apparatus, extending the calculation to arbitrary screening strengths. They recast published MICROSCOPE measurements by projecting the Earth-induced dark matter wake onto the satellite's sensitive orbital and spin frequency bands.
key_results: Recasting MICROSCOPE's SUEP and SUREF sensor data probes scalar dark masses up to $m_{	ext{DM}}  8 	imes 10^{-9}	ext{ eV}$ and couplings below the supernova SN1987A bound.
Including additional frequency sidebands is projected to extend the mass reach to $m_{	ext{DM}}  7 	imes 10^{-8}	ext{ eV}$ and probe regions below BBN constraints.
Confirmed that amplitudes inferred independently from SUEP (different compositions) and SUREF (identical compositions) agree within twice their combined uncertainty.
summary.why_it_matters: Relevant to your interest in precision atomic and nuclear probes of new physics, ultralight scalar dark matter, and novel signatures in precision space-based instrumentation.
summary.caveats: The analysis relies on an idealized concentric spherical mass distribution model for the satellite bus and sensor hardware because complete engineering blueprints are publicly unavailable.

papers.title: Exothermic Higgs portal: from LUX-ZEPLIN recoil to Gamma Rays
papers.abstract: We show that a minimal extension of the Standard Model (SM) by a single complex scalar $\phi$ provides a viable inelastic exothermic, thermal relic, interpretation of the recently reported nuclear-recoil candidate from LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ). The mass terms and Higgs-portal interactions split $\phi$ into two nearly degenerate real scalars, $\phi_{1,2}$. For mass-splitting of a few hundred keV, $\phi_2$ is cosmologically long-lived and the two states have comparable relic abundances. Taking $\phi_{1,2}$ masses to be $\sim100\,$GeV, with off-diagonal Higgs coupling fixed by relic abundance, the exothermic down-scattering yields an order-one event expectation for the LZ exposure, without relying on the high-velocity tail of the dark matter velocity distribution required in endothermic scenarios. This scenario can be tested using different nuclear targets and with indirect dark matter searches: $\phi_2\to\phi_1\gamma\gamma$ decays give a broad sub-MeV photon continuum that can be probed by INTEGRAL/SPI and COSI; $\phi_1\phi_2$ annihilation produces a GeV-scale continuum, extending up to $\sim$100 GeV, that is probed by Fermi-LAT observations of dwarf galaxies; current CMB constraints are satisfied and annihilation among dark matter particles captured in the Sun is strongly suppressed. Next-generation experiments could probe correlated scattering, decay, and annihilation signatures of this thermal Higgs-portal scenario.
papers.reason: Presents an exothermic Higgs portal complex scalar dark matter interpretation of the LZ nuclear recoil anomaly with direct, indirect, and collider signatures. [favorite author: Zupan]

summary.tldr: A minimal Higgs-portal extension of the Standard Model with a complex scalar provides a thermal exothermic dark matter explanation for the LUX-ZEPLIN nuclear-recoil candidate while satisfying indirect and solar constraints.
summary.novel_idea: Unlike endothermic scenarios requiring high-velocity halo tails, exothermic down-scattering ($	ext{	extchi}_2 A 	o 	ext{	extchi}_1 A$) utilizes an existing population of the heavier degenerate scalar state ($	ext{	extchi}_2$) to naturally yield high recoil energies ($	extsim 250	ext{ keV}$) without extreme kinematic suppression.
summary.method: The authors solve coupled Boltzmann equations for thermal freeze-out of coannihilations to fix the off-diagonal Higgs coupling $g  0.05$ for a $	extsim 100	ext{ GeV}$ mass and $	extsim 600	ext{ keV}$ splitting. They evaluate xenon recoil spectra using chiral-EFT nuclear response functions and test parameter spaces against INTEGRAL/SPI, Fermi-LAT dwarf galaxies, CMB, and solar capture/annihilation limits.
key_results: Yields an order-one event expectation ($0.5	ext{--}2	ext{ events}$) for the $2.84	ext{ tonne-year}$ LUX-ZEPLIN exposure at the candidate recoil energy ($E_R = 248	ext{ keV}$).
Radiative decays $	ext{	extchi}_2 	o 	ext{	extchi}_1 	ext{	extgamma}	ext{	extgamma}$ produce a sub-MeV photon continuum testable by future COSI observations.

Solar capture is dominated by exothermic $	ext{	extchi}_2 A 	o 	ext{	extchi}_1 A$ scattering, leaving captured dark matter mostly in the lighter state and suppressing solar neutrino signals from mixed annihilation well below IceCube bounds.
summary.why_it_matters: Intersects low-energy dark matter searches (LZ), nuclear-recoil physics on xenon targets, and electroweak/Higgs-portal EFT frameworks relevant to your core interest in low-energy neutrino and rare-process precision physics.
summary.caveats: The predicted xenon recoil spectrum is highly sensitive to the momentum dependence of the nuclear response near diffraction minima (e.g., Helm form factor versus chiral EFT calculations yield different efficiency-weighted event totals).

papers.title: New Scaling Relations for Nucleons in Three-Nucleon Short-Range Correlations
papers.abstract: The search for three nucleon short range correlations~(3N- SRCs) in nuclei is one of the intensive areas of research in high density nuclear physics. It is in part motivated by the prediction of the above two-solar mass neutron stars based on 3N short-range forces and the subsequent observation of such stars. The 3N-SRCs serve as a "laboratory" for probing the dynamics of largely unknown irreducible 3N-forces. However, the identification of 3N-SRCs in high energy nuclear processes is still elusive making the prospects of their investigation problematic. In this work we introduced new dynamical parameters for 2N- and 3N- SRCs, $\beta_{2N}$ and $\beta_{3N}$ respectively, which characterize the strength of SRCs beyond combinatorial counting of nucleons in SRCs. For 2N-SRCs the introduction of $\beta_{2N}$ parameter resulted in a previously known and experimentally verified relation for proton and neutron momentum distributions in 2N-SRCS. For 3N-SRCs the $\beta_{3N}$ parameter allowed to factorize momentum distributions of nucleons in the correlation resulting in a prediction of a new scaling relation between proton and neutron momentum distributions in 3N SRCs. This relation, if valid gives a new venue for identification of 3N-SRCs in electro-nuclear processes. Even though the obtained scaling relation is relevant in the relativistic domain, the possibility of separating center of mass motion of SRCs on the light-front allows to check the validity of predicted scaling using non-relativistic ab-initio wave functions. We found surprisingly reasonable confirmation of our prediction analyzing ab-initio wave functions of nuclei in the range $3\le A\le 12$. This indicates the robustness of the scaling relation and opens up a new direction in searching for 3N-SRCs experimentally.
papers.reason: Introduces new dynamical parameters $ eta_{3N}$ for 3N-SRCs and predicts new scaling relations for nucleon momentum distributions, directly relevant to neutrino-nucleus interaction modeling.

summary.tldr: New dynamical SRC parameters $ eta_{2N}$ and $ eta_{3N}$ enable the factorization of nucleon momentum distributions, leading to a new scaling relation for three-nucleon short-range correlations (3N-SRCs).
summary.novel_idea: Unlike 2N-SRCs where $pn$-dominance allows straightforward factorization, 3N-SRCs involve mixed $ppn$ and $pnn$ configurations that spoil simple combinatorial scaling. The authors introduce dynamical strength parameters $ eta_{2N}$ and $ eta_{3N}$ that go beyond combinatorics, successfully deriving a universal scaling relation for proton and neutron momentum distributions in 3N-SRCs.
summary.method:
The authors construct light-front momentum distributions for $j$-nucleon SRCs and define the dynamical parameters $ eta_{jN}$ to isolate local interaction dynamics. They test the resulting scaling relations against non-relativistic ab-initio variational Monte Carlo (VMC) wave functions (using AV18, Norfolk NV2+3-Ia chiral potentials, Urbana-X, and TM' 3N forces) and Faddeev calculations for nuclei in the range $3 
eq A 
eq 12$.
key_results: Derived a new scaling relation between proton and neutron momentum distributions for 3N-SRCs, valid for light-front momentum fractions $\alpha \gtrsim 1.6$ ($p \gtrsim 700$ MeV/c).
Ab-initio checks across $3 \le A \le 12$ confirm that the scaled $n_p/n_n$ ratios converge to unity in the 3N-SRC domain with $\le 8\%$ disagreement for nuclei like $^6$He and $^9$Li.
Demonstrated that the predicted scaling is largely insensitive to specific models of 3N nuclear forces, confirming that $\beta_{3N}$ captures the dominant local dynamics.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly relevant to neutrino-nucleus interaction modeling and generators (like GENIE, NuWro, and GiBUU) by providing a rigorous way to constrain high-momentum tails and nuclear wave function treatments at kinematics relevant to short-range correlations and cross-section analyses.
summary.caveats: The derivation uses an input parameter $r \approx 0.8$ characterizing the ratio of majority to minority components in 3N-SRCs, which assumes isospin symmetry and neglects $nnn/ppp$ configurations.

papers.title: Matching $\nu$2HDM onto $\nu$SMEFT up to one-loop accuracy
papers.abstract:
The neutrinophilic two-Higgs-doublet model ($
u$2HDM) represents one of the most economical extensions of the Standard Model (SM) while still giving rise to a rich phenomenology. In this work, we carry out a full tree-level and one-loop matching of this ultraviolet completion onto the SM Effective Field Theory extended with right-handed neutrinos ($
u$SMEFT), including all operators up to mass dimension six. This is achieved by integrating out the heavy scalar doublet at a scale well above the electroweak scale. For the matching procedure, we employ the functional method in combination with the naive dimensional regularization and modified minimal subtraction schemes. After converting from the Green's basis to the minimal, non-redundant Warsaw-extended basis, the effects of high-scale new physics are encoded in the Wilson coefficients of both physical and evanescent operators in the $
u$SMEFT. These coefficients are given in terms of the $
u$2HDM parameters prior to spontaneous symmetry breaking. Our final expressions at the high-energy matching scale are provided as ancillary files on \href{https://github.com/dufewe/v2HDM-to-vSMEFT}{GitHub}. This setup forms the foundation for forthcoming systematic and global analyses of the $
u$2HDM parameter space using effective field theory techniques.
papers.reason: Performs full tree and one-loop matching of the neutrinophilic 2HDM onto nuSMEFT at dimension six, highly relevant to precision EFT and neutrino mass models.

summary.tldr: A complete tree-level and one-loop matching of the neutrinophilic two-Higgs-doublet model ($\nu$2HDM) onto the $\nu$SMEFT up to mass dimension six has been performed.
summary.novel_idea:
The heavy scalar doublet of the $
u$2HDM is consistently integrated out prior to electroweak symmetry breaking using modern functional methods, bridging the high-scale UV parameters directly to the Warsaw-extended $
u$SMEFT basis including evanescent operators.
summary.method: Employs the functional matching approach via python packages (Matchmakereft, Matchete, STrEAM, and SuperTracer) in naive dimensional regularization (NDR) and the $	ext{\overline{MS}}$ scheme. Field redefinitions, equations of motion, and one-loop Fierz transformations / Greek reductions are applied to map Green's basis operators to the non-redundant Warsaw-extended basis.
key_results: Derived complete matching expressions for Wilson coefficients of dimension-5 and dimension-6 physical and evanescent operators in $\nu$SMEFT in terms of pre-SSB $\nu$2HDM parameters.
Cataloged all non-zero evanescent Wilson coefficients for four-fermion operators at one-loop order under NDR.
Published explicit matching formulas as ancillary GitHub files to support future global EFT fits of $\nu$2HDM parameter space.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly supports EFT workflows for low-energy precision physics, SMEFT/LEFT matching, and neutrino non-standard interactions (NSI) when right-handed neutrinos are treated as active dynamical degrees of freedom.
summary.caveats: The resulting expressions assume a decoupling and alignment limit where the heavy scalar mass scale $\Lambda^2 = m_{22}^2$ is well above the electroweak scale.

papers.title: Active-subspace learning reveals dominant parameter directions in nuclear observables
papers.abstract: Nuclear observables computed using ab initio methods can depend on many low-energy constants (LECs) of the underlying chiral effective field theory interactions, while being sensitive to only a few LEC combinations. We use active-subspace learning to identify these dominant parameter directions directly from many-body calculations. For ground-state energies and charge radii of oxygen isotopes, we find that more than 99% of the gradient-based variation is concentrated along a single direction for each observable in the 17-dimensional LEC space. Comparing these directions across nuclei and observables quantifies similarities in their LEC dependence. The same analysis yields derivative-based global sensitivities without requiring a global emulator. Active-subspace directions can also serve as an efficient representation for emulation, greatly improving Gaussian-process emulators especially for broad LEC variations. We demonstrate this for Hartree-Fock calculations of $^{48}\mathrm{Ca}$, where the emulator error is improved with active-subspace learning by more than two orders of magnitude.
papers.reason: Applies active-subspace learning to identify dominant parameter directions of chiral EFT low-energy constants in ab initio nuclear calculations.

summary.tldr: Active-subspace learning reveals that more than 99% of gradient-based variations in nuclear ab initio observables are concentrated along a single direction in the 17-dimensional chiral EFT LEC space.
summary.novel_idea: Applying active-subspace learning (ASL) directly to many-body calculations of oxygen isotopes bypasses the need for global emulators when extracting dominant parameter directions and derivative-based global sensitivities.
summary.method: Calculated gradients of IMSRG ground-state energies and charge radii of oxygen isotopes with respect to 17 chiral LECs using nearest-neighbor approximations. Constructed the gradient covariance matrix $\mathbf{C}$ and performed eigenvalue decompositions to identify active versus inactive subspaces.
key_results: The normalized first eigenvalue for $E(^{16}\text{O})$ is $\overline{\lambda}_1 = 0.998$, indicating that the 17-dimensional LEC dependence is effectively one-dimensional.

Gaussian-process (GP) emulator errors for $^{48}$Ca Hartree-Fock calculations are reduced by more than two orders of magnitude (RMSE dropping from $143.67$ MeV to $0.59$ MeV) when input spaces are rotated using ASL prior to kernel fitting.
Demonstrated that dominant active directions computed for $^{16}$O strongly align across other oxygen isotopes (angles $< 10^\circ$).
summary.why_it_matters: Provides a powerful tool for nuclear structure and ab initio electroweak response calculations, drastically improving uncertainty quantification and surrogate model efficiency for expensive many-body solvers.
summary.caveats: Derivative-based global sensitivity measures (DGSM) serve as approximations to global Sobol indices and remain tied to the specific sampled parameter domain.

papers.title: Cryogenic performance of Silicon Photo-Multipliers at LN$_2$ temperature and at 3 K in the RES-NOVA cryostat
papers.abstract: Silicon Photo-Multipliers (SiPMs) are semiconductor-based photodetectors that offer performance comparable to that of traditional Photo-Multiplier Tubes (PMTs), while providing several advantages, including low operating voltage, immunity to magnetic fields, compact size, and mechanical robustness. These features have led to their widespread adoption in scintillator-based detectors for both fundamental and applied physics. In recent years, there has been a growing interest in the detection of scintillation light at cryogenic temperatures in low-temperature experiments based on bolometric detectors, such as RES-NOVA and CUPID, as well as in emerging quantum applications. In the RES-NOVA experiment, radiopure PbWO$_4$ crystals are used to detect supernova neutrinos. The scintillation of PbWO$_4$ can only be evaluated at cryogenic temperatures, as the scintillation light yield is negligible at room temperature. We present measurements of the performance at cryogenic temperatures of Hamamatsu S13360-1350CS SiPMs in terms of breakdown voltage and gain, at 77~K (in a liquid nitrogen bath) and at 3~K. The cooling down to 3~K has been carried out using a Proteox LX cryostat from Oxford Instruments.
papers.reason: Measures cryogenic performance (gain and breakdown voltage) of SiPMs down to 3 K for low-temperature bolometric detectors targeting supernova neutrinos in RES-NOVA and CUPID.

summary.tldr: Characterization of Hamamatsu S13360-1350CS SiPMs demonstrates stable cryogenic performance down to 3 K in a dilution refrigerator for low-temperature scintillation detectors.
summary.novel_idea: Provides precise cryogenic measurements of SiPM breakdown voltage and gain at 77 K and down to 3 K using an Oxford Instruments Proteox LX cryostat, validating photosensors for cryogenic lead tungstate ($	ext{PbWO}_4$) scintillating bolometers.
summary.method: Tested Hamamatsu S13360-1350 SiPMs using a climatic chamber ($-50^\circ\text{C}$ to $+25^\circ\text{C}$), a liquid nitrogen bath (77 K), and an Oxford Instruments dilution refrigerator (3 K). Extracted breakdown voltages from I-V curves and single-photon gain spectra via a CAEN SP5600 readout kit.
key_results: The breakdown voltage $V_{\text{bd}}$ decreases from $\sim 51.5$ V at room temperature to $\sim 41.5$ V at 77 K.
Confirmed that the breakdown voltage reaches a plateau and remains constant at $\sim 41.5$ V when cooled further from 77 K down to 3 K.
Verified that dark count rates scale down appropriately with lowered temperatures.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly supports low-energy neutrino instrumentation (specifically the RES-NOVA supernova neutrino experiment using cryogenic $	ext{PbWO}_4$ crystals) and low-temperature detector developments like CUPID.
summary.caveats: Optical excitation tests were omitted inside the liquid nitrogen bath, and planned tests at an intermediate 38 K thermal stage require improved thermalization verification.

papers.title: A Multi-messenger Study of the Cygnus bubble
papers.abstract: We perform a comprehensive investigation of particle acceleration at the termination shocks of massive star clusters, with a particular focus on the Cygnus region. Building on the particle-acceleration model for cluster-driven winds, we use recently available spectral and spatial measurements of ultra-high-energy $\gamma$-rays from the Cygnus bubble to place stringent constraints on the physical conditions in the acceleration zone. By jointly modelling the observed $\gamma$-ray spectrum and spatial morphology, we derive quantitative limits on key parameters such as the maximum particle energy, acceleration efficiency, magnetic-field strength, and shock geometry, and assess their consistency with a hadronic origin of the emission. These data allow us to refine the target gas profiles within and around the bubble, thereby improving estimates of the expected hadronic $\gamma$-ray and neutrino fluxes. Using this revised gas model, we compute the neutrino emission associated with the Cygnus bubble and evaluate the statistical significance of a potential neutrino signal from this region for current and near-future high-energy neutrino observatories. Taken together, these results provide a more precise characterisation of the particle-acceleration environment at cluster termination shocks and help clarify the role of young massive star clusters as potential Galactic PeVatrons and contributors to the observed diffuse high-energy neutrino and $\gamma$-ray emissions.
papers.reason: Jointly models ultra-high-energy gamma rays and computes hadronic neutrino fluxes from the Cygnus bubble, highly relevant for galactic PeVatrons and neutrino observatories.

summary.tldr: A multi-messenger study of the Cygnus bubble using a stellar-wind termination shock model shows that Bohm-type diffusion successfully explains UHE $\gamma$-ray spectra and is compatible with IceCube neutrino observations.
summary.novel_idea: Jointly models the spatial morphology and UHE $\gamma$-ray spectrum of the Cygnus bubble (incorporating an updated gas density profile from atomic, molecular, and ionized tracers) within a Bayesian framework to test different particle diffusion regimes at cluster termination shocks.
summary.method: Used the Nautilus Bayesian fitting module to constrain cluster wind parameters ($u_{\text{sw}}$, $\dot{M}_*$, $\rho_0$, $\mathcal{T}_{\text{age}}$, $s$, $\eta_B$, $\epsilon_{\text{cr}}$) against Fermi-LAT, HAWC, ARGO, and LHAASO data under Kolmogorov, Kraichnan, and Bohm diffusion assumptions, subsequently computing expected all-flavor neutrino fluxes for IceCube and KM3NeT.
key_results: Bohm-type diffusion yields the lowest reduced chi-squared ($\chi^2_{\text{red}} = 6.16$) and successfully reproduces both the SED and LHAASO surface brightness profiles.

Kolmogorov diffusion is strongly disfavored ($\chi^2_{\text{red}} = 31.88$), while Kraichnan diffusion requires extreme, physically challenging wind luminosities ($\mathcal{L}_{\text{sw}} \approx 2.83 \times 10^{39} \text{ erg s}^{-1}$).
The derived hadronic model predictions align with reported neutrino excesses from the Cygnus region in IceCube data, supporting the hadronic PeVatron interpretation.
summary.why_it_matters: Relevant to high-energy astrophysical neutrino sources, cosmic-ray acceleration mechanisms, and galactic background characterization for neutrino telescopes like DUNE and IceCube.
summary.caveats: Assuming pure Bohm diffusion across the entire bubble is an upper-limit idealization, and the model slightly underpredicts the highest-energy ($>100$ TeV) surface brightness data at the outer edges.

papers.title: Behavior of the zero modes in the Light-front for pseudo scalar particles: pion case
papers.abstract: Light-front Quantum Field Theory (LFQFT) stands as an optimal framework for delving into the intricate substructure of hadronic bound states. In this study, we employ a Light-Front Constituent Quark Model (LFCQM) to investigate the pion's internal structure. This model has previously demonstrated significant success in describing the properties of pseudoscalar mesons. A crucial consideration within the light-front formalism is the dependence on the chosen reference frame, stemming from the explicit breaking of covariance. Herein, we meticulously analyze the contribution of zero modes to the pion's electromagnetic current. Subsequently, we explore the impact of these zero modes on observable quantities, including electromagnetic form factors, the pion's electromagnetic radius, and its weak decay constant, $f_\pi$. Furthermore, we comprehensively investigate the behavior of zero modes and their dependence on both the momentum transfer, $Q^2$, and the model's intrinsic parameters, such as constituent quark masses ($m_{(q,\bar{q})}$) and the regulator mass ($m_R$). Our findings reveal a substantial dependence of light-front zero modes on the specific frame employed for the calculation of the electromagnetic current. Interestingly, we observe that the maximal contribution of the zero mode occurs at a specific four-momentum transfer, denoted as $Q^2 = -q^2 = q_Z^{2(Max.)}$.
authors: J. Pacheco B. C. de melo
papers.reason: Analyzes the contribution and behavior of zero modes in the light-front constituent quark model for pion electromagnetic currents and form factors, highly relevant to hadron structure.

papers.title: Heavy-quark limit of $B$-meson distribution amplitudes in light-front holography with longitudinal confinement
papers.abstract: The heavy-quark limit of light-front holographic wave functions for heavy--light mesons is investigated, with particular emphasis on the leading-twist $B$-meson light-cone distribution amplitude, $\phi_B^+(\omega)$. Two prescriptions for incorporating finite quark masses are compared: the invariant mass ansatz (IMA) and the longitudinal confining framework based on the Li--Maris--Zhao--Vary (LMZV) potential. In the IMA, although the peak of the distribution amplitude remains at a soft spectator momentum, its characteristic width decreases as $\Delta\omega \propto m_B^{-1/2}$ in the heavy-quark limit, causing the longitudinal distribution to collapse asymptotically to $\delta(\omega-m_q)$. Accordingly, the inverse moment approaches the finite limit $\lambda_{B,\mathrm{IMA}} \to m_q = \mathcal{O}(\Lambda_{\mathrm{QCD}})$. In contrast, the LMZV framework approaches a finite leading-power (LP) profile with a stable width of order $\mathcal{O}(\Lambda_{\rm QCD})$ and a stable inverse moment, $\lambda_{B,\mathrm{LMZV}}^{\mathrm{LP}} = m_q + \sigma/2 = \mathcal{O}(\Lambda_{\mathrm{QCD}})$, which is independent of the heavy-quark mass. The heavy-quark scaling of $f_B$ is also examined using the local axial-vector current at zero transverse separation. While the LMZV longitudinal wave function has a non-singular heavy-quark limit, the bare light-front current does not reproduce the canonical heavy-quark effective theory scaling $f_B \propto m_B^{-1/2}$: the decay constant scales as $f_B \propto m_B^{-1}$ in the LMZV framework and as $f_B \propto m_B^{-5/4}$ in the IMA. Thus, a non-singular heavy-quark limit of the longitudinal wave function is necessary but insufficient to ensure the correct heavy-quark scaling of local current matrix elements without systematic current matching.
papers.reason: Investigates the heavy-quark limit of B-meson light-cone distribution amplitudes using light-front holography and longitudinal confinement frameworks.

papers.title: Accounting for correlations in the $\omega\pi$ spectral function and its implication on the leading model dependent contribution to the $\tau^- \to \pi^-\pi^0 \nu_\tau\gamma$ decay
papers.abstract:
The $\omega\pi$ spectral function, measured in the decay $	au^- 	o \pi^-\omega
u_	au$ by the CLEO Collaboration, is described in the vector meson dominance approach. We sample the parameter space using a Metropolis Monte-Carlo algorithm and generate a set of parameters of the corresponding form factor, explicitly accounting for the correlation among them. We show the improvement in the uncertainty region of the spectral function with respect to neglecting correlations. We test the conserved vector current hypothesis by showing the agreement of the spectral function with the expected from the measurement of the cross section of $e^+e^- 	o \omega\pi$ by the SND experiment, and the consistency of the branching ratio of the $	au^- 	o \pi^-\omega
u_	au$ decay with the value reported by the Particle Data Group. As an application, we consider the $\omega$-channel of the $	au^- 	o \pi^-\pi^0
u_	au\gamma$ process, the leading model dependent contribution in the vector meson dominance approach. We compute the contribution to the long distance electromagnetic correction function $G_	ext{EM}(t)$, of the pure $\omega$-channel and its interference with the structure independent part. We show that the uncertainties, using the set of correlated parameters, are largely reduced with respect to neglecting correlations. The implication on the isospin symmetry breaking correction to the muon magnetic dipole moment estimation from tau data is found to be consistent with previous results but with improved precision.

papers.title: Heavy-meson molecules with dynamical pions
papers.abstract: We investigate heavy-meson molecules by treating the pion as a dynamical degree of freedom. We construct an energy-independent Hamiltonian that couples the two- and three-body Fock spaces. The two-body sector contains a pseudoscalar meson and a vector meson $H_1H_2^{*}$, while the three-body sector consists of two pseudoscalar mesons and a pion $H_1H_2 \pi$. The $H^*$ self-energy, the $H_1H_2^{*}$ pion-exchange interaction, and the $H_1H_2\pi$ three-body propagation are consistently generated through the coupling between the two Fock sectors. We use the Gaussian expansion and complex scaling methods to solve the coupled Schr\"odinger equation. Previous approaches usually reduce three-body effects to energy-dependent two-body kernels and solve the equations iteratively. Our approach obtains the poles by solving a single linear generalized eigenvalue problem. The eigenvectors also provide explicit wave functions in both Fock sectors, allowing a qualitative analysis of channel weights and spatial structure. We benchmark the framework in $T_{cc}^{+}$ and $X(3872)$. The benchmark results are consistent with the current experimental pole determinations. We then apply this formalism to the $BB\pi$, $B\bar{B}\pi$, $DB\pi$ and $D\bar{B}\pi$ systems. We predict one isoscalar bound state in each of these systems. The $DB\pi$ and $D\bar{B}\pi$ systems also contain resonances lying below and above their three-body threshold, respectively. We propose complementary searches for these resonances through $DB^*\to DB\gamma$ and $D\bar B\pi$. This coupled Fock-space framework can be readily extended to other few-body systems in which unstable constituents can decay and change the particle number.
papers.reason:
Investigates heavy-meson molecules ($T_{cc}^+, X(3872), BB ar{B} ar{
u}$, etc.) by coupling two- and three-body Fock spaces with dynamical pions using complex scaling.

papers.title: Thermal Festina Lente
papers.abstract: According to the Festina Lente bound, particles charged under a $U(1)$ gauge field cannot be too light. Otherwise, the largest charged black holes of de Sitter space would discharge in a way that leads to a crunching singularity in violation of cosmic censorship. The Festina Lente bound has previously been extended to also include a background of thermal radiation, but where vacuum energy still dominates cosmic evolution, which imposes a maximal temperature $T\leq T_{\max}=(cV/\sigma)^{1/4}$. We extend this analysis by accounting for thermal enhancement of the discharge process and making the analysis more quantitative. The result is a bound $m\gtrsim\ell (cV/\sigma)^{1/4}$ on the masses of charged particles. Here, $\ell$ is a term that depends logarithmically on the gauge coupling and particle charge. At weak coupling this leads to a significantly stronger constraint than the $\sqrt{gq}$ scaling of the original Festina Lente bound. As a result, the present vacuum energy requires every particle of charge $10^{-26}\lesssim gq\lesssim e$ to be heavier than $0.03$--$0.2$ eV, provided its gauge boson is lighter than the Hubble scale. An unbroken gauged $B-L$ with Dirac neutrinos gives $m_{\nu,{\rm lightest}}\gtrsim10$--$43$ meV for $10^{-29}\lesssim g_{B-L}\lesssim10^{-24}$, in tension with the DESI DR2 limit once $g_{B-L}\gtrsim7\times10^{-28}$. The same limit bounds a neutrino millicharge to $\epsilon_\nu\lesssim2\times10^{-27}$. We also revisit the Standard Model effective field theory constraints from the electroweak phase transition. During slow-roll inflation the Standard Model electron violates the bound over the whole range of Hubble rates allowed by the CMB tensor limit and by nucleosynthesis, unless the photon is Higgsed, its coupling is suppressed, or one considers very fine-tuned versions of Higgs inflation.
papers.reason: Extends the Festina Lente bound to thermal backgrounds, deriving direct lower bounds on neutrino masses and millicharges from vacuum energy constraints.

papers.title: Experimental Searches for Muon to Electron Conversion in Nuclei
papers.abstract: Charged lepton flavor violation (CLFV) provides a highly sensitive probe of physics beyond the Standard Model. This experimental review discusses $\mu^{-} \to e^{-}$ conversion in nuclei, which is a muon CLFV process characterized by a clean monoenergetic-electron signature and the ability to exploit large samples of stopped muons. It describes the physics motivation, basic experimental principles, key background sources, and search strategies, as well as the status and prospects of past and next-generation experiments such as COMET and Mu2e. Future experimental concepts may extend the sensitivity even further. If a signal is observed, comparisons among results obtained with different target nuclei and with those from complementary searches for other muon CLFV decay modes will be essential for identifying the underlying interaction.
papers.reason: Provides a comprehensive review of muon-to-electron conversion in nuclei as a prime probe of physics beyond the Standard Model.

papers.title: Strong vertex $N N \rho$ in dense medium
papers.abstract: We investigate the strong coupling form factors associated with the $NN\rho$ interaction vertex in nuclear matter using the QCD sum rule framework. These form factors are calculated incorporating the in-medium modifications of the relevant condensates and operators into the operator product expansion (OPE) for the first time. We analyze the behavior of the strong form factors as functions of the momentum transfer squared and density of medium and evaluate the corresponding strong couplings at the on-shell point of the $\rho$ meson at nuclear saturation density. Then we extend the analyses to get information at higher densities. Our results provide complementary information on the in-medium $NN\rho$ interaction and may be useful for phenomenological, experimental and observational studies of dense hadronic matter.
papers.reason: Calculates in-medium modifications to the NNrho strong coupling form factors using QCD sum rules at nuclear saturation and higher densities.

papers.title: Role of the GPD-$E$ in exclusive dijet electroproduction at the Electron-Ion Collider
papers.abstract: We calculate the contribution of the $E$-type generalized parton distributions (GPDs) to exclusive dijet electroproduction in $ep\to e'jjp$ in collinear QCD factorization, including both the proton helicity-flipping amplitude and the GPD-$E$ term in the helicity-conserving amplitude, using the double distribution approach for modeling. We include light sea and valence-quark exchanges as well as gluon exchanges and compare the proton helicity-conserving and helicity-flipping contributions for HERA-energy phase space and for Electron-Ion Collider (EIC) kinematics. We find that the helicity-flipping cross section is dominated by valence-quark exchange and has a markedly different dependence on $|t|$ and $x_{\mathbb P}$ from the helicity-conserving contribution. In the EIC kinematics considered here, the helicity-flip contribution becomes comparable to the helicity-conserving one at large $|t|$ and $x_{\mathbb P}$. The results show that exclusive dijet electroproduction can be sensitive to the $E$-type GPDs in the kinematic region accessible at the EIC.
papers.reason: Calculates the contribution of E-type GPDs to exclusive dijet electroproduction at EIC kinematics, tying directly to nucleon structure probes.

papers.title: Light nucleus and hypernucleus production at RHIC and LHC energies: a comparative study of phenomenological models
papers.abstract: This document summarizes the work of the EMMI Rapid Reaction Task Force on ``Understanding light (anti)nuclei production at RHIC and LHC'', which took place at GSI on 8--12 April 2024. The meeting brought together experimentalists and theorists to discuss the current understanding of light-nuclei and hypernuclei production in high-energy hadronic collisions, with particular emphasis on statistical hadronization, coalescence, kinetic, and transport approaches. The discussions addressed the experimental status and the ability of different theoretical descriptions to reproduce the available measurements, as well as the connections between nuclear production, femtoscopic correlations, source sizes, nuclear wave functions, and the formation dynamics of loosely bound states. This document reviews the main experimental and theoretical developments presented during the RRTF, summarizes the key questions that emerged from the discussions, and identifies observables and future measurements that may help discriminate among different production mechanisms.
papers.reason: Summarizes current phenomenological understanding and model comparisons for light nuclei and hypernuclei production in high-energy collisions.

papers.title: The Skin Detector System of the LZ Dark Matter Experiment
papers.abstract: This paper presents the design, calibration, and performance of the Skin Detector component of the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) dark matter experiment. The Skin Detector consists of approximately 2 tonnes of liquid xenon instrumented with 131 photomultiplier tubes, surrounding the central time-projection chamber and functions as an active veto system for background rejection. Energy calibration with monoenergetic gamma sources established a position-dependent energy scale and determined prompt and delayed veto thresholds. Radon decays in the Skin can be identified with less than 15~mm spatial resolution, revealing stable convective flow patterns with measured velocities ranging from 2-4 mm/s that persisted throughout extended data-taking periods. The achieved Skin veto threshold meets or exceeds the design goal of 100~keV throughout the Skin volume. The prompt veto efficiency for gamma rays emitted following electron capture in $^{127}$Xe is found to be ($88 \pm 2$)\%, consistent with the simulated value of ($90.4 \pm 0.6$)\%. M-shell EC decays are used to validate the LZ detector sensitivity for low-mass dark matter during the first science run.
authors: M. G. D. van der Grinten
papers.reason: Details the design, calibration, and background rejection performance of the liquid xenon Skin Detector in the LUX-ZEPLIN dark matter experiment.

papers.title: Characterization of Next Generation Power Over Fiber Systems under Cryogenic Conditions for Advanced Physics Instrumentation
papers.abstract: The successful application of Power-over-Fiber (PoF) technology to power photon detection systems in DUNE prototypes operating under high-voltage and cryogenic conditions has laid the groundwork for the next generation of PoF systems operating in harsh environments. This paper presents the characterization of the main components of a new PoF system operating at 1470 and 1550 nm, including the measurement of the electrical-to-optical conversion efficiency of laser transmitters, the optical-to-electrical conversion efficiency of commercial optical power converters (OPCs), and the estimation of optical fiber attenuation under cryogenic conditions. In addition, a detailed characterization of the response of silicon photomultipliers (SiPMs) to light leakage from optical fibers and OPCs is presented, using 808 nm as a reference to evaluate the reduction in the SiPM response at longer wavelengths. The results of this work provide a foundation for the development of next-generation PoF systems capable of powering electronics and electrical systems for future high-energy physics experiments. In addition, the electrical isolation, low-noise operation, and long-term reliability of PoF technology could motivate its application in other research fields requiring remote power delivery under cryogenic conditions, as well as in systems where infrared photons could affect their performance.
papers.reason: Characterizes power-over-fiber systems and SiPM responses under cryogenic and high-voltage conditions directly relevant to DUNE photon detection instrumentation.

papers.title: Hidden Neutrino Active Galaxy Candidates: Prospects for Catalog and Stacking Searches with IceCube, IceCube-Gen2, and KM3NeT
papers.abstract: In high-energy neutrino astrophysics, the identification of high-energy neutrino sources is a central goal, and jet-quiet active galactic nuclei (AGNs) have emerged as promising candidates. For this purpose, we present a theory-guided, intrinsic X-ray selected sample of hidden neutrino AGN candidates consisting of $28$ X-ray bright AGNs (X-HiNAC), combining the {\em Swift}/BAT and BASS surveys with dedicated {\em NuSTAR} observations and spectral analyses. We compile their intrinsic X-ray fluxes, spectral properties, luminosity distances, and supermassive black hole masses, to provide a coherent sample for neutrino source searches. The sample is physically motivated but remains model independent given that the neutrino flux is proportional to the intrinsic X-ray flux. Using the magnetically powered corona model, we also demonstrate the prospects for individual-source and stacking searches with IceCube-Gen2 and KM3NeT. We identify promising individual targets and find that stacking the remaining sources, excluding NGC 1068, could yield a $5\sigma$ detection within $\sim 5-15$ years under favorable model assumptions at the current and upcoming neutrino observatories. We highlight systematic uncertainties in the adopted source parameters, particularly the black hole masses, for which different measurement techniques can yield estimates differing by up to an order of magnitude. Such uncertainties can significantly affect the predicted neutrino emission, motivating more precise black hole mass measurements and improved broadband X-ray observations. Our findings motivate improved multiwavelength characterization of nearby AGNs and provide a guide for investigating their role as high-energy neutrino sources.
papers.reason: Constructs an X-ray selected sample of hidden AGN candidates to evaluate stacked high-energy neutrino source prospects for IceCube, IceCube-Gen2, and KM3NeT.

papers.title: Probing the charm-quark dead cone effect in heavy ion collisions
papers.abstract: The first experimental study of the dead-cone effect for the charm quark in heavy ion collisions is presented. The analysis is based on a sample of lead-lead (PbPb) collisions at a center-of-mass energy per nucleon pair of 5.02 TeV, recorded by the CMS experiment at the CERN LHC in 2018 and corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 1.7 nb$^{-1}$. The studied observable is the angular distribution of hard, collinear intrajet emissions that are selected with the late-$k_\mathrm{T}$ grooming algorithm. The analysis is performed using inclusive jets and a sample of jets containing prompt D$^0$ mesons. The angular distribution of late-$k_\mathrm{T}$ emissions in PbPb collisions is found to be shifted towards larger angles in D$^0$ jets relative to inclusive jets, indicating a suppression of collinear splittings for D$^0$ jets. This shift, which is expected from the dead-cone effect, is consistent with a similar observation made in proton-proton collisions. The new measurement disfavors hypotheses that predict a filling of the charm-quark dead cone by medium-induced radiation in heavy ion collisions.
papers.topic: Charm Dead Cone in Heavy Ions
papers.reason: Measures the charm-quark dead-cone effect in PbPb collisions at the LHC, providing essential baseline data for heavy-flavor parton shower and jet quenching dynamics.

papers.title: Precision determination of $B_c$ and $B_c^*$ meson decay constants from lattice QCD
papers.abstract: We present a lattice QCD study of heavy-heavy meson decay constants using the HISQ gauge ensemble generated by the MILC Collaboration. Employing the HISQ action for both charm and bottom valence quarks tuned to their physical masses, we determine pseudoscalar, vector, and tensor decay constants for heavy quarkonium and $B_c$ systems. Preliminary results are presented for the decay constants of the $B_c$, $B_c^*$, $\eta_c$, $\eta_b$, and $\Upsilon$ mesons.
papers.reason: Computes precision $B_c$ and $B_c^*$ meson decay constants from lattice QCD using HISQ gauge ensembles, directly aligning with precision flavour and lattice inputs.

papers.title: 2+1 flavor light hadron spectrum with PACS10 configurations
papers.abstract: We present the results for the hadron spectrum, the pseudoscalar meson decay constants, and the quark mass ratio in the continuum limit using the ``PACS10'' gauge configurations generated with the $O(a)$-improved Wilson quark action and the Iwasaki gauge action. Numerical simulations are carried out at three lattice spacings keeping the space-time volumes over (10 fm$)^4$ in 2+1 flavor QCD at the physical point. We calculate physical quantities with two choices of conventions to define pseudoexperimental values expected in the isosymmetric QCD. In order to investigate the finite size effects on the physical quantities we have additionally generated the (5.4 fm$)^4$ lattice at the coarsest lattice spacing of $a=0.08487(14)$~fm, which is a hypercube with half the length in each direction compared to the PACS10 configurations. While the finite size effect is hardly observed in comparison of the hadron effective masses on the (10.9 fm$)^4$ and (5.4 fm$)^4$ lattices, the results for the pseudoscalar meson decay constants show discrepancies beyond the error bars. The (5.4 fm$)^4$ lattice also serves for determining the expansion parameters of the pseudoscalar meson masses and decay constants, and the octet baryon masses in terms of the quark masses around the physical point with the aid of the mass reweighting technique. The expansion parameters are used for the fine-tuning of the physical point employing the pseudoexperimental masses of the $\pi$ meson, $K$ meson, and the $\Xi$ baryon as physical inputs in each convention. We compare the results for the octet baryon masses and the pseudoscalar decay constants in the continuum limit with the corresponding pseudoexperimental values in both conventions. We also discuss the deviation between two results with different conventions. As for the quark mass ratio the result is compared with the recent FLAG summary.
papers.reason: Presents a high-precision 2+1 flavor light hadron spectrum and decay constants in the continuum limit from PACS10 large-volume lattice configurations.

papers.title: Axion polarimetry with parametric readout: photon-number conversion and sensitivity limits
papers.abstract: We propose a bias-assisted active photon-number conversion scheme for axion-induced polarization rotation in a four-port optical ring cavity with parametric readout. A calibrated real polarization rotation applied \emph{before} the final optical parametric oscillator (OPO) converts the otherwise quadratic response of the summed output photon number into a linear signal. We derive the resulting photon moments and the extracted-field covariance, retaining the four-port optical transfer, finite axion coherence and linewidth. Our principal phenomenological result is a prospective low-mass sensitivity window at $m_a=10^{-18}$--$10^{-16}\,\mathrm{eV}$, extending below the published exclusion bounds included in our comparison, notably the NuSTAR M82 limits. This is a conditional noise-equivalent projection, using the adopted $A/\sigma_A=1$ stochastic-power criterion and a parameterized technical-noise budget, not a confidence-level exclusion forecast. As a separate readout result, OPO-based total counting reduces the noise-equivalent coupling by approximately $5\%$ relative to matched selective attenuation in a favorable higher-frequency band; $5\%$ internal loss together with a $0.10$-rad pump-phase offset leaves a $3.5\%$ advantage in the stated example. A coherent input with only the final OPO retains this high-frequency benefit, whereas optimized coherent polarimetry remains more sensitive in the baseline. Our results identify both the operating principle of active number conversion and the stability requirements for a future implementation.
papers.reason: Proposes an active photon-number conversion scheme with parametric readout for axion polarimetry, offering novel dark matter detection concepts with astrophysical context.

papers.title: Search for $\mathrm{GeV}$-scale axion-like particles in PbPb collisions
papers.abstract: A search is performed for the production of axion-like particles with masses in the range 3-10 GeV using PbPb collision data recorded by the LHCb experiment, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of $0.228~\mathrm{nb}^{-1}$ and a nucleon-nucleon centre-of-mass energy of $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=5.02$ TeV. This is the first search for axion-like particles produced exclusively by two photons ($\gamma\gamma\to a\to\gamma\gamma$) in the forward direction. It extends sensitivity to previously unexplored regions of the parameter space, probing axion-like particle masses and couplings down to 3.0 GeV and $3.2\times10^{-4}~\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$, respectively. This result provides the most stringent limits to date on the production of axion-like particles from exclusive photon-photon fusion processes with masses between 3 and 5 GeV.
authors: U. De Freitas Carneiro Da Graca
papers.reason: Searches for GeV-scale axion-like particles using photon-photon fusion in PbPb collisions at LHCb, relevant to BSM portal searches. [favorite author: Jordy de Vries]

papers.title: Evidence for the decay $B^0 \to \mu^+ \mu^-$ and improved measurements of the decay $B^0_s \to \mu^+ \mu^-$
papers.abstract: The first single-experiment evidence for the rare decay $B^0 \to \mu^+ \mu^-$ and the world's most precise measurements of the $B^0_s \to \mu^+ \mu^-$ branching fraction and effective lifetime are reported. The results are obtained using Run 3 proton-proton collision data corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 18 fb$^{-1}$ recorded with the LHCb Upgrade I detector at a centre-of-mass energy of $13.6$ TeV between 2024 and 2025. Their combination with the Run 1 and Run 2 LHCb results further improves the precision. All measurements are found to be in agreement with the Standard Model expectations.
authors: U. De Freitas Carneiro Da Graca

papers.title: Unitarity and Positivity Constraints on C- or P-odd Anomalous Quartic Couplings
papers.abstract: In this work, we provide a comprehensive study of partial-wave unitarity and positivity constraints in the dimension-eight genuine anomalous quartic gauge coupling (aQGC) sector of the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT). We extend previous partial-wave unitarity analyses to include all C- or P-odd operators, thereby completing the coverage of the full basis of 34 operators. We also derive an analytical set of necessary forward-limit positivity bounds that include all CP-odd Wilson coefficients. We demonstrate that non-vanishing CP-odd Wilson coefficients require non-vanishing contributions from the CP-even sector to satisfy the derived positivity conditions. Combining the positivity conditions with partial-wave unitarity, we obtain stronger bounds on twenty-three of the thirty-four Wilson coefficients in this sector of the SMEFT.
papers.reason: Derives partial-wave unitarity and positivity constraints on dimension-eight aQGCs in SMEFT, highly relevant to precision EFT work.

papers.title: Interacting scalar-fermion two-component dark matter in a gauged $\boldsymbol{U(1)_{B-L}}$ model
papers.abstract: We propose an interacting two-component dark matter model based on a gauged $U(1)_{B-L}$ extension of the Standard Model, which also accommodates neutrino masses through the type-I seesaw mechanism. The dark sector consists of a Dirac fermion $\chi$ and a complex scalar $S$, which can both be stable without imposing an additional discrete symmetry and are directly coupled by a gauge-invariant Yukawa interaction. The resulting conversion, semi-conversion, and semi-annihilation processes lead to a genuinely coupled freeze-out. After imposing collider and dark matter constraints, we identify viable solutions away from the $Z'$ resonance for both mass hierarchies, $m_S > m_\chi$ and $m_S < m_\chi$. Despite the strong direct-detection constraints, part of the surviving parameter space remains within the reach of next-generation experiments.
papers.reason: Proposes a gauged $U(1)_{B-L}$ scotogenic model with interacting two-component dark matter and neutrino mass generation.

papers.title: Top quark couplings at the muon collider
papers.abstract:
We present an overview of the sensitivity of a muon collider to the flavor-diagonal electroweak couplings of the top quark, using dimension-six operators of the Warsaw basis. Of the nine fermion-boson operators involving the top quark, the bounds on three are not competitive with existing limits, and we focus on the remaining six. We estimate individual $95\%$ CL limits on the corresponding Wilson coefficients at $\sqrt{s} = 3$, $6$, $10$, and $14$~TeV from $2\sigma$ statistical cross-section uncertainties, and assess the effect of an assumed systematic uncertainty. We consider six top-quark production modes: $t ar t$, $t  ar t h$, $t  ar t 
u  ar 
u$, $t  ar t \mu^+ \mu^-$, single-top $t ar b \mu^-  ar 
u_\mu$, and single-top-plus-Higgs, the last three for several rapidity coverages of the final-state muons. The $s$-channel $t ar t$ and $t ar t h$ processes give the strongest sensitivity to the electroweak dipole couplings, with allowed intervals narrower than the current LHC ones by factors of about $3$ to $6$ at $\sqrt{s} = 3$ and $6$ TeV, and by an order of magnitude or more at $10$ and $14$ TeV. The left- and right-handed $ttZ$ couplings, as well as the Yukawa $tth$ couplings (for $\sqrt{s} \geq 6$ TeV), are best probed in $t  ar t 
u  ar 
u$ production, while the right-handed $tbW$ coupling is best probed in single-top production. For the $ttZ$ and $tbW$ couplings, the limits improve on the current LHC bounds by factors from about $1.5$ to more than an order of magnitude. Our results agree with previous analyses of the Yukawa and the dipole couplings, and provide a roadmap for more in-depth studies.
papers.reason: Evaluates muon collider sensitivities to flavor-diagonal electroweak top quark couplings using dimension-six Warsaw basis operators.

papers.title: Sensitivity of the IceCube atmospheric muon rate to decadal trends in the effective atmospheric temperature
papers.abstract: Decadal changes in the Antarctic stratosphere, generally associated with ozone recovery and shifts in polar circulation, are of broad geophysical interest. However, independent long-term measurements of the atmosphere above the Antarctic interior are scarce. We assess whether the atmospheric muon rate recorded by IceCube could constrain decadal changes in the effective atmospheric temperature, $T_\mathrm{eff}$, a weighted average of temperature through the atmosphere that is most sensitive to the stratosphere. Using public atmospheric reanalysis data and records of cosmic-ray, solar, and geomagnetic variability, we reproduce the measured seasonal response of the IceCube muon rate. We then test whether the same response applies to long-term temperature changes with a different vertical temperature profile. The limiting requirement is detector stability rather than counting statistics: an unmodeled muon rate drift of $1\%\,\mathrm{decade^{-1}}$ would mimic a temperature trend of $2.8\,\mathrm{K\,decade^{-1}}$. The long-term rate must therefore be stable to approximately $0.3\%\,\mathrm{decade^{-1}}$. Within this budget, snow accumulation contributions can be constrained. For a 14-year record, atmospheric variability gives a one-sided 95% CL statistical sensitivity of $1.6\,\mathrm{K\,decade^{-1}}$. Given this sensitivity, the $\sim0.9\,\mathrm{K\,decade^{-1}}$ cooling indicated by the 2011-2025 atmospheric records would become distinguishable after approximately 30 years of measurement.
papers.reason: Assesses the sensitivity of IceCube's atmospheric muon rate to decadal stratospheric temperature trends, relevant to IceCube systematics and atmospheric neutrino fluxes.

papers.title: From Kination to Detection: Scotogenic Scalar Dark Matter
papers.abstract: We investigate scalar dark matter in the scotogenic model during an early kination-dominated epoch. The enhanced expansion rate causes earlier freeze-out and increases the relic abundance, opening viable dark matter masses from approximately $200~\mathrm{GeV}$ to $1~\mathrm{TeV}$ while reducing the need for co-annihilation with a nearly degenerate singlet fermion. Current indirect searches strongly constrain the $(100-200)~\mathrm{GeV}$ region, whereas much of the surviving parameter space can be probed by CTA and next-generation direct detection experiments. The viable spectra also lead to complementary collider signatures, including missing transverse energy, displaced leptons, and disappearing charged tracks, providing promising tests at the HL-LHC and future lepton colliders.
papers.reason: Explores scalar dark matter in the scotogenic model during an early kination-dominated epoch with collider and direct detection signatures.

papers.title: Measurement of the $\lvert V_\mathrm{cb}\rvert$ element of the CKM matrix using $\mathrm{t\bar{t}}$ events in pp collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV
papers.abstract: A measurement of the magnitude of the Cabibbo$-$Kobayashi$-$Maskawa matrix element $V_\mathrm{cb}$ is presented using top quark pair events produced in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV. The data correspond to an integrated luminosity of 138 fb$^{-1}$ collected by the CMS experiment at the LHC. The measurement targets the lepton+jets final state, where one W boson decays leptonically and the other hadronically. The value of $\lvert V_\mathrm{cb}\rvert$ is extracted from the branching fraction of the W $\to$ cb decay. To identify this rare signal amid the dominant W $\to$ ud and W $\to$ cs backgrounds, a multivariate discriminant based primarily on the b jet tagging information of the jets assigned to the hadronic W boson decay is used. The measured value is $\lvert V_\mathrm{cb}\rvert$ = [4.59$^{+0.44}_{-0.48}$ (stat) $^{0.64}_{-0.76}$ (syst)] $\times$ 10$^{-2}$. This measurement provides a complementary determination of $\lvert V_\mathrm{cb}\rvert$ at the electroweak scale, independent of the nonperturbative quantum chromodynamics inputs used in measurements based on semileptonic B meson decays.
papers.reason: Measures the CKM matrix element $|V_{	ext{cb}}|$ using $t ar{t}$ events at CMS via $W	o cb$ decays, offering an independent electroweak-scale determination.

papers.title: Resolving the Two-Fold Ambiguity in Tau Momentum Reconstruction via a Self-Consistent Weighting Method
papers.abstract: The reconstruction of $\tau$ lepton momenta in $e^{+}e^{-} \to \tau^{+}\tau^{-}$ processes suffers from a two-fold kinematic ambiguity due to undetected neutrinos. We show that the common practice of retaining both solutions with equal weight systematically biases the extracted angular coefficients: the bias grows with the size of the $\cos^{2}\theta$ modulation of the production distribution $f(\cos\theta)$, but remains resolvable even in the nearly uniform QED limit at the $\psi(2S)$ threshold. We propose a self-consistent weighting method based on a fixed-point theorem: assigning normalized weights $w_{i} = f(\cos\theta_{i})/[f(\cos\theta_{1})+f(\cos\theta_{2})]$ yields a weighted distribution $h(x) = f(x)[1+\varepsilon(x)]$ with $\varepsilon(x) \ll 1$ under a detailed balance condition. Monte Carlo simulations at $\sqrt{s}=3.686$~GeV and $4.8$~GeV show that the fixed-point iteration converges to the true angular coefficient $\alpha$ within statistical uncertainty, providing a robust framework for angular analysis without event-by-event ambiguity resolution.
papers.reason: Resolves the two-fold kinematic ambiguity in tau momentum reconstruction via a self-consistent fixed-point weighting method, highly relevant to tau neutrino and lepton analyses.

papers.title: Holographic study of the scalar meson $K_0^*(1430)$ with dynamical longitudinal confinement
papers.abstract: Within the framework of light-front holographic QCD, where transverse confinement is inherently realized through holography, the structure and mass spectrum of the light scalar meson $K_0^{*}(1430)$ are investigated by employing the invariant mass ansatz and enhancing the model with a longitudinal confinement potential (specifically, the 't Hooft equation and the analytically solvable LMZV potential). The combined transverse and longitudinal confinement dynamics lead to more reliable calculations of key observables, including decay constants, parton distribution function, $\xi$-moments, and twist-$2$ and twist-$3$ distribution amplitudes. Transition form factors for the semileptonic decay $B \rightarrow K_0^{*} \ell^+ \ell^-$ are computed from these amplitudes, yielding predictions for differential branching ratios and longitudinal lepton polarization asymmetries as functions of $q^2$. The results are compared with other theoretical models, offering valuable insights into the non-perturbative dynamics of QCD. The predicted observables provide theoretically motivated benchmarks for future experimental investigations of $B\rightarrow K_0^*(1430)\ell^+\ell^-$ decays at LHCb and Belle II.

papers.title: A General Manifestly Covariant Construction of Partial-Wave Amplitudes in the Rarita-Schwinger Formalism
papers.abstract: We propose a new set of functions, named Relative Spin Wave Functions (RSWFs), defined via covariant pure boosts to a common rest frame. RSWFs separate spin transport from orbital-spin coupling while preserving the conventional partial-wave angular structure in a manifestly covariant form. Within the Rarita-Schwinger formalism, this approach generates explicit, covariant on-shell partial-wave amplitudes for two-body decays of massive particles of arbitrary spin, with definite orbital angular momentum and total final-state spin. This general framework provides a foundational Lorentz basis for hadronic reaction studies and $LS$-organized operators in theoretical investigations, such as Lattice QCD and QCD sum rules.
papers.reason: Constructs a manifestly covariant partial-wave amplitude framework using Relative Spin Wave Functions in the Rarita-Schwinger formalism for hadronic reactions and Lattice QCD inputs.

papers.title: Gravitational form factors of the baryon octet and flavor dependence in an NJL quark--diquark model
papers.abstract: We calculate the gravitational form factors of the baryon octet in a proper-time-regulated Nambu--Jona-Lasinio quark--diquark model using the total energy--momentum tensor. The momentum, angular-momentum and stress form factors reveal different flavor dependences, and the momentum and stress slope radii follow distinct hierarchies. With the diquark pole inputs taken from the hadron-spectrum calculation, the $\Sigma$ is more compact than the nucleon in its momentum response but more extended in its normalized stress response; it also has the smallest magnitude of the forward stress form factor. This combination of weaker forward strength and larger normalized extent persists under separate variations of the scalar and axial-vector diquark couplings. Along a self-consistent flavor-breaking path the initially degenerate radii split, and the sampled $\Sigma$--nucleon stress-radius ordering changes while the momentum ordering does not. The metric continuation and external pole inputs further change these hierarchies. Together, the octet form factors show how flavor breaking and scalar and axial-vector correlations affect momentum and stress differently.
papers.reason: Calculates gravitational form factors of the baryon octet in an NJL quark-diquark model, examining flavor dependence and stress radii.

papers.title: Impact on Final-State Bulk Observables in Heavy-Ion Collisions from an Extended MC Glauber Model of Quantum Rotors
papers.abstract: Nuclear structure is closely connected to anisotropic flow in central heavy-ion collisions (HICs), so flow observables provide important probes for constraining nuclear deformation. Conventional Monte Carlo (MC) models typically describe deformed nuclei as classical rotors with definite orientations, whereas the ground states of even--even nuclei with $J=0$ are rotationally invariant. Motivated by the importance of rotational symmetry restoration, we systematically investigate symmetric collisions involving the representative even--even nuclei $^{20}\mathrm{Ne}$, $^{28}\mathrm{Si}$, $^{96}\mathrm{Ru}$, and $^{238}\mathrm{U}$ using an extended MC Glauber model that incorporates quantum superposition of nuclear orientations. In the final state, the quantum treatment suppresses elliptic flow $v_2\{2\}$, with the strongest effect observed in ultra-central Ne+Ne collisions. Quantum superposition further induces system-dependent changes in normalized symmetric cumulants and shifts the Pearson correlation between $v_2^2$ and $[p_T]$ toward the corresponding near-spherical reference values. Moreover, the quantum treatment modifies cross-system flow ratios and the U+U/Au+Au covariance ratio used experimentally to constrain nuclear deformation parameters. Our results suggest that the quantum-rotor treatment may affect the interpretation of nuclear structure information inffered from heavy-ion collision final-state observables.
papers.reason: Extends the MC Glauber model with quantum superposition of nuclear orientations to study heavy-ion final-state flow observables and nuclear deformation.

papers.title: On-shell constituent approach to the light-front partonic energy-momentum tensor
papers.abstract: The forward matrix elements of the energy-momentum tensor in momentum space, parameterized by gravitational transverse-momentum distributions (TMDs), provide a microscopic window into hadronic mechanical structure. While the longitudinal and transverse columns match to canonical vector TMDs up to twist-4, the light-front minus column involves the unintegrated parton energy $k^-$, leaving this sector undetermined in general quantum chromodynamics. Working within relativistic light-front constituent frameworks where active quarks are modeled as effective on-shell quasiparticles, we show that this energy factorizes algebraically. This establishes a closed matching relating all 32 gravitational TMDs to canonical vector TMDs up to twist-4, including target polarization and T-odd final-state interactions. This completion provides access to the light-front energy density and its transverse Sivers dipole distortion, demonstrates the local equivalence between convective energy and momentum transport velocities, and determines the longitudinal normal stress. Comparing longitudinal and transverse stresses yields a boost-invariant anisotropy ratio that charts the mechanical crossover from collinear confinement dominance to transverse isotropic balance. While formulated within the constituent approximation, these results offer baseline insights into the three-dimensional continuum mechanics of the nucleon.
papers.reason: Uses an on-shell constituent approach to derive a closed matching between gravitational TMDs and vector TMDs up to twist-4 for nucleon mechanics.

papers.title: Search for dark photon dark matter near $\mathbf{1\,meV}$ using a superconducting mixer
papers.abstract: We demonstrate the use of a superconducting mixer for direct searches for dark photon dark matter (DPDM) in the meV mass range. DPDM couples to the ordinary electromagnetic field through kinetic mixing with a coupling constant $\chi$ and can convert into ordinary photons at the surface of a metal plate. For DPDM masses of 1 meV, the conversion photons have frequencies of around 240 GHz. At such frequencies, superconducting mixers enable low-noise spectroscopic measurements. We performed a direct search for DPDM in the mass range 1.0047578-1.0047598 meV, corresponding to the frequency range 242.94935-242.94983 GHz, using approximately one hour of data obtained with a cryogenic millimeter-wave receiver based on a superconducting mixer. No significant excess was found, and we set upper limits of $\chi < (1.6\text{-}1.9)\times10^{-9}$ at the 95% confidence level.
